- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if history shows mean reversion.
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00) are common; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 2x recent mean.
- Model often overreacts to sentiment shifts in 3–7 day horizon; apply smoothing or decay factor to sentiment-weighted adjustments.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 day pullback after spike), reduce forecast momentum in next 5–10 days.
- For 10+ day horizons, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation), model may misread trend; use sentiment average as baseline for correction.
